title: Pre-registered prediction for the Gemma-2-9B run
status: REGISTERED - not yet tested (9B run pending, needs cluster)
exactly_provable_identity: For balanced concatenation, the mass-mean combined direction is exactly the (norm-weighted) average of the constituent mass-mean vectors: theta_combo = 1/2 (theta_A + theta_B).
Hence the combined-MM SCORE is exactly the average of the constituents' scores: theta_combo . x = 1/2 (theta_A . x + theta_B . x). This is the ONLY part that is provable.
empirical_predictions_motivated_by_the_i: NOT provable from the identity (AUROC is a rank statistic, nonlinear in scores): the following are EMPIRICAL predictions the identity motivates, to be tested, not derived.

In-distribution is protected: on T = A or T = B the native constituent contributes the correct sign and, on easily-separable data, AUROC saturates -> combined MM works in-distribution regardless of cos(theta_A, theta_B). (The narrower 'antipodal -> in-distribution collapse' guess was FALSIFIED at 2B; see falsified_predictions.)

Cross-topic fails by sign-cancellation: on a THIRD dataset T, if A transfers inverted while B transfers aligned, the averaged scores cancel -> collapse toward chance. (Observed at 2B: cities+neg_cities->neg_sp MM 0.399 = avg of cities->neg_sp 0.000 and neg_cities->neg_sp 0.979.)
LR is NOT constrained to the average; it searches for a jointly-separating direction, so it should be far less sensitive to cos(theta_A, theta_B).
REFINED_mechanism_antipodal_is_the_failu: CORRECTION: orthogonal is NOT the failure mode. Averaging two ORTHOGONAL unit vectors gives a vector at 45deg to each, norm reduced by sqrt(2) -- rotated but NOT degenerate, still a usable direction. Averaging two ANTIPODAL vectors gives near-cancellation; the surviving residual is NOISE-DOMINATED. Antipodal is the failure mode.

This fits all four MM rows of Table 2 with the Fig 3 geometry, 3 for 3 including the scale flip: (a) cities+neg_cities orthogonal -> NIE IMPROVES both scales (.77->.85 @13B, .58->.81 @70B); (b) larger+smaller @13B antipodal -> NIE COLLAPSES (.71->.26); (c) larger+smaller @70B common direction -> NIE HOLDS (.67->.66). Explains exactly M&T's flagged dissociation (combined training helps cities but hurts larger_than).

DIRECTIONAL, not norm: M&T normalize theta so adding it maps mean-false->mean-true (probe-value space), so intervention strength is rescaled. The failure therefore CANNOT be 'small norm' -- it is that after near-cancellation the surviving DIRECTION is not the causally-implicated one, so scaling it up injects noise rather than flipping the judgment. (Earlier 'degenerate small-norm' framing was WRONG under a normalizing protocol.)

REFINED PREDICTION (registered): combined-MM NIE degradation (vs the better singleton) is MONOTONE in the proximity of cos(theta_A, theta_B) to -1. Antipodal -> degrades; orthogonal -> preserved; aligned -> preserved.

2B TEST (geometry already MEASURED, not inferred): cos(larger,smaller)=-0.62 (antipodal-ish) and cos(cities,neg_cities)=-0.02 (orthogonal) at L13. So predict: combined larger+smaller shows DEGRADED NIE vs larger_than alone; combined cities+neg_cities does NOT degrade vs cities alone. Classification half already shown (larger+smaller combined MM 0.99 own-held-out despite cos -0.62), so a NIE drop reproduces M&T's classification-vs-NIE dissociation WITHIN 2B.
scope_and_the_actual_MnT_puzzle: READ FROM THE ACTUAL PDF (pypdf, not summarizer). Table 2 = NIE. MM rows [13B f->t, t->f | 70B f->t, t->f]: cities .77/.90|.58/.89; cities+neg_cities .85/.97|.81/.95; larger_than .71/.79|.67/1.01; larger+smaller .26/.53|.66/1.03; likely .70/.54|.68/.27.

The PRECISE puzzle is the paragraph before 7.1 (p9): 'Training on datasets and their opposites helps for cities but not for larger_than [NIE], ... surprising, considering probes trained on larger+smaller are MORE ACCURATE on sp_en_trans than larger alone (App D).' => a CLASSIFICATION-vs-NIE DISSOCIATION: combined training improves larger+smaller CLASSIFICATION but HURTS its NIE (13B .71/.79 -> .26/.53). The 7.1 sentence itself is imprecise ('poorly poorly' typo) and does not cleanly match Table 2 at 70B; anchor on the precise pre-7.1 statement.

WHAT THE MECHANISM SHOWS (classification side, done at 2B): theta_combo = 1/2(theta_A+theta_B); for antipodal constituents (larger+smaller) theta_combo is a degenerate small-norm average that STILL classifies fine because AUROC saturates on rank (2B: larger+smaller combined own-held-out 0.99 despite cos_AB -0.62).

CANDIDATE ANSWER TO THE DISSOCIATION (needs NIE to confirm): the same degenerate theta_combo, once normalized as an INTERVENTION vector, is causally wrong -> poor NIE. So combined training can improve classification (rank saturates) while hurting NIE (direction degenerate). This directly targets M&T's stated dissociation.

TO CONFIRM: run M&T's fully-specified intervention protocol (Section 6.1) and measure NIE along theta_combo vs theta_single for larger_than (antipodal) and cities (non-antipodal). LOW design risk: the protocol (few-shot 'This statement is: TRUE/FALSE', theta normalization p(mu- + theta)=p(mu+), NIE formula) is documented, unlike induced_lies.csv.

POSSIBLE NO-70B CLOSURE: the score-averaging identity is scale-free; M&T Fig 3 independently reports 70B constituent geometry; M&T Table 2 reports 70B NIE. If the 2B NIE experiment shows combined-MM NIE tracks constituent alignment, then mechanism + their reported geometry predicts their reported NIE pattern without a 70B run. Rests on Table 2/Fig 3, now read from the actual PDF.
independent_reproductions_of_MnT: Task B (cities/neg_cities rotate antipodal->orthogonal with depth at 2B) reproduces M&T App C (LLaMA-2-13B: antipodal early -> orthogonal mid -> aligning late). 2B did not reach the aligning phase within 26 layers.
Task C (cities+neg_cities improves generalization to neg_sp_en_trans) reproduces M&T p7 ('training data containing not improves generalization on other negated statements').
predictions_for_9b: P1: Combined-MM CROSS-DATASET generalization quality is a MONOTONE INCREASING function of cos(theta_A, theta_B) of the constituent directions, measured at the evaluated layer. Aligned constituents -> good combined generalization; orthogonal/antipodal -> poor.
P2: LR combined-training generalization is substantially LESS sensitive to cos(theta_A, theta_B) than MM (LR succeeds across a wider range of constituent geometries).

P3 (M&T 7.1 reconciliation): Per M&T Fig 3, larger_than/smaller_than move from antipodal (13B) toward a COMMON direction (70B) with scale, while datasets<->negations stay approximately orthogonal (Fig 3c). So at 9B expect cos(theta_larger, theta_smaller) to be LESS antipodal / more positive than at 2B, and cos(theta_cities, theta_neg_cities) to remain near-orthogonal. Where cos(A,B) rises above ~0, combined-MM cross-transfer for that pair should improve toward LR's level.
P4: The MM<->LR gap on hard cross-topic negation (cities+neg_cities -> neg_sp_en_trans) will shrink at 9B IF cos(theta_cities, theta_neg_cities) rises; it will persist if that cos stays near 0.
falsification_criteria: If combined-MM cross-dataset generalization at 9B does NOT track cos(theta_A, theta_B) (e.g. MM generalizes well cross-topic even when constituents are orthogonal), the averaging mechanism is wrong.
If LR is just as sensitive to cos(theta_A, theta_B) as MM, the MM-specific averaging-constraint story is wrong.
falsified_predictions: FALSIFIED at 2B (do not repeat): 'antipodal constituents -> MM combined training fails even IN-DISTRIBUTION.' larger+smaller combined MM scored 0.98-1.00 on its own held-out at L11/13/15 despite cos_AB -0.52 to -0.71, because the pairs are not perfectly antipodal (norm_ratio 0.38-0.49) and AUROC saturates on easily-separable data. In-distribution is protected; only cross-topic transfer exposes the averaging failure.

anchor_2b_layer13.note: At 2B/L13 no constituent pair is aligned (all cos < 0), so the aligned/positive-cos regime that M&T report at 70B is exactly what the 9B run is needed to reach and test.
